about: The topic-resolution eval set (M5). Written before the resolver exists, on purpose: M3's eval found three bugs on its first run because its cases were written to fail, and a case written after the code tests what was built rather than what was asked for.
topic: the free text a user types. The resolver turns it into candidate instruments with a confidence and a rationale (PRD FR-10); the user confirms.

expect.must_include: every listed symbol must appear among the resolver's candidates. It is a floor, not the whole answer - a resolver that also offers QCOM for semiconductors is not wrong, so extra candidates are not penalised here. What a sensible upper bound on candidates is belongs to the resolver, not to this file. When a topic resolves to several interpretations (see app/topics/resolution.py), a case is judged on the interpretation holding the most expected symbols - the list the user would see after choosing that meaning.

expect.resolves_to_nothing: the topic is outside what any instrument universe can answer, and the resolver must say so rather than offer its least-bad candidates. The same lesson as /ask's relevance floor: a nonsense query must not return three plausible-looking rows.

author: 'user' cases were written by the product's user on 2026-09-24, before any resolver code existed and without reading the corpus or the code. They are the held-out set MEMORY.md asked for, and the most valuable cases in the file. 'session' cases were written by the Claude session that will also write the resolver, and carry exactly the bias the ask.json disclosure describes.
as_written: the user's line verbatim. Kept so that any correction made to a case is visible as a correction rather than silently becoming what the user said.
retired_symbols: tickers that no longer trade under that name. A case must not expect one - the resolver could never return it, so the case would fail forever and teach everyone to ignore the eval.

The user-short-* cases are the same user's phrasings of how a topic is actually typed, added 2026-09-24 at the session's request. The long labels read like category names; nobody types 'Weight Loss Drugs & Obesity Therapeutics' into a search box.

threshold_fitting_topics: what the resolver's candidate count and confidence bands are fitted to, written by the session on 2026-09-24 BEFORE any similarity was measured. No case may repeat one (test_topic_eval_set_contract.py), for the reason ask.json gives: an eval that reuses the fitting data measures nothing and looks exactly like a pass.

sealed: true marks the user's second batch (2026-09-24), written after the first run and handed over before any fix to it. run_topic_eval.py skips sealed cases unless --unseal is passed, and they were not run until the ranking and disambiguation changes were final. Once unsealed and run, they are ordinary cases - a seal only holds once.

Known before unsealing: LVMUY trades only OTC in the US, and the universe screens primary exchanges, so that case cannot pass as written. It is left as the user wrote it; the runner reports such a symbol as 'not in universe', distinct from ranked too low. 'Data Centers & Infrastructure REITs' is also close in meaning to the fitting topic 'data center real estate', so the NOTHING_BELOW line has seen a near-paraphrase of it.

threshold_fitting_topics.ambiguous: words with two unrelated market meanings (snacks or web tracking; metals or crypto; oil or software; sea freight or parcels), added by the session before measuring, to fit the disambiguation rule. The in_domain topics double as its negatives: a rule that calls 'gold mining' ambiguous is wrong.

UNSEALED 2026-09-24, after M5 slice 2 (ETF holdings) was final. Result on the sealed batch: 1/11 cases and 14/35 expected tickers - identical for the slice-1 resolver and the slice-2 resolver run against the same universe, so the holdings signal as built did not generalise to topics it was not developed against. The batch is no longer held out: anything tuned after this date has seen it, and a claim of held-out performance needs a new batch written by someone who has not seen these results.

SQ.note: Block, Inc. moved its NYSE ticker from SQ to XYZ in January 2025. Checked 2026-09-24: Yahoo returns no instrument for SQ and 'Block, Inc.' for XYZ.
